notes: Actual receipts and disbursements for calendar year 2024, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report (cash basis). Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school corporations with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collects property and local income taxes for every government in the county and pays them over; that money is left out.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
Money the county holds for others or passes through (tax settlements, payroll and clearing accounts, trusts and escrow; $74,210,731 received) is left out.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Indiana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.detail: The Putnam County Sheriff's Department operates three Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

notes: Actual receipts and disbursements for calendar year 2024, as the township reported them in its Annual Financial Report (cash basis). Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school corporations with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Putnam County.
Indiana townships cover the whole county, cities and towns included; the township trustee provides poor relief and, in many townships, fire protection.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
Money the township holds for others or passes through (tax settlements, payroll and clearing accounts, trusts and escrow; $4,091 received) is left out.
Distributions to other governments ($25,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 2 license-plate cameras are mapped inside Greencastle Township's borders in OpenStreetMap (1 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Indiana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 1 Flock Safety license-plate camera is mapped inside Greencastle Township's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
